definitions.text: Passengers per flight are the seats per flight times the load factor.
Contribution per flight is the passengers times the fare plus extras per passenger, less the flight's variable cost.
A route's annual contribution is its contribution per flight times its flights per year.
Contribution is route revenue less the variable costs of flying: fuel, crew, maintenance, and landing and airport fees.
Operating profit is total contribution less fixed costs: aircraft leases, hub facilities and corporate overhead.
The revenue a fare cut costs each flight is the fare reduction times the passengers per flight.
The breakeven fare is the flight's variable cost divided by its passengers, less the extras per passenger.
The breakeven load factor is the share of seats that must be filled for fare plus extras per passenger to cover the flight's variable cost.
The contested routes' share of contribution is their combined prior-year contribution divided by the network's.
The gain from redeploying is the new routes' annual contribution plus the losses removed by exiting the contested routes.

definitions.term: first-year contribution on a new route
definitions.text: First-year contribution per flight on a new route uses the first-year load factor in place of the planned one.
